title: Mums of autistic girls create special app for parents

input.lead: Kate Dunn and Nisha Warburton wanted to enable parents to connect and feel less isolated
input.summary: Kate Dunn and Nisha Warburton wanted to enable parents to connect and feel less isolated
input.evidence_text: Two mothers who created an app to help parents of children with special needs connect hope it means no one will feel alone Kate Dunn, who's daughter Ophelia has non-verbal autism and ADHD, met the mother of Sophia, also diagnosed with autism, Nisha Warburton, in a carpark outside their specialist nursery in Bolton, Greater Manchester Nisha said: "You go from feeling like the only person who is dealing with such a situation to recognising that actually a lot of people are." In their free time, or while their children were asleep, the pair decided to make the app, called SEN2gether, to create a community as well as to share information and tools for parents With almost 2,000 sign-ups within its first month, the pair have created a growing private community of parents and carers where they can share what works, ask questions as well as find local connections and guidance "We are just mums. We do not have a background in business or digital app making but what we notice is people love it and recognise it, and we are growing and developing it everyday," Nisha said

title: Manchester City Council says e-scooter trial could begin in 2027

input.lead: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
input.summary: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
input.evidence_text: People in Manchester could be travelling around on a fleet of electric scooters next year after plans for a new trial were announced Manchester City Council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027, although the authority added it had not yet considered an operator for the e-scooters The plans come off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford Council said had been a major success A council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trial had not yet been made, and was conditional on backing from Greater Manchester Police and other groups They said provisional approval had been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and "officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester" Summer 2027 was the latest a trial could start in line with DfT requirements for new trials, they added

Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. input.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade.
